messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGING: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2 — incident id inc-2026-03-15-01. Trigger: 5m error rate > 10%. Pager: Jay (oncall).

Jay (oncall): I'm on it. Initial hypothesis: routing layer or a model kernel crash. Jay (oncall) grabbing logs and scaling history.

Alice M: Noted. I'm pulling LB and gateway traces now. Any customer-facing hits observed yet? Sophie (support) — can you scan support queue for recent P0s?

Sophie (support): Quick scan — two customers reporting timeouts for embeddings and generation started ~10:30 UTC. I flagged both as incident-impacted. Escalating to SalesOps.

Ben K: I see a spike of `KV cache OOM` followed by many retries in runtime logs around 10:29:12 UTC. Pushing tail of logs here:```
[2026-03-15T10:29:12.123Z] runtime: kv_cache_alloc failed: out_of_memory
[2026-03-15T10:29:12.456Z] model_worker: restart attempt 1 pid=2345
[2026-03-15T10:29:13.789Z] gateway: upstream 502 from worker pid=2345 route=/v1/generate
```

Carlos: Thanks Ben. Can you paste the kernel mismatches and any recent deploys? EngInfraBot, any kernel rollouts in the last 24h?

EngInfraBot: No scheduled kernel rollouts in last 24h. Autoscaler did a fast scale-up at 10:28:50 UTC due to sudden load.

Jay (oncall): Adding timeline notes (rough):
- 10:28:30 UTC: sustained qps increase on gen endpoints (burst from a key customer test)
- 10:28:50 UTC: autoscaler scales pool up (fast)
- 10:29:12 UTC: worker kv cache OOM -> worker restarts -> 502s
- 10:30:00 UTC: errors peak at 18% for /v1/generate in us-west-2
- 10:34:30 UTC: partial mitigation: evict cache and force warm workers; errors drop to ~4%

Alice M: Can we confirm if the autoscaler launched machines with different GPU driver/kernels? Ben — the `kv_cache_alloc` suggests memory accounting issue maybe aggravated by quantization changes.

Ben K: No driver changes. I see a recent model load that used a new quantized artifact around 09:00 UTC. Not sure it's related but model variant might increase KV memory footprint.

Sophie (support): Draft status page blurb: "We are investigating elevated error rates for text generation in our us-west-2 region. Some customers may experience timeouts or 5xx errors. Engineers are actively mitigating; no PII or data loss suspected. Updates to follow." Thoughts? @Elena (PM)

Elena (PM): Good start. Add ETA and customer actionability: tell customers to retry and that we are enabling fallback model variants to reduce memory pressure. Draft suggestion: "Mitigation: enabling compatible fallback model variant and evicting KV caches. Expected restoration window: 15–30 minutes."

Jay (oncall): OpsRunner, please coordinate the fallback roll and monitor key customers (IDs: acct-1224, acct-997). Also start a short bridge with SCs.

OpsRunner: On it. Starting canary fallback to lighter quantized model on 10% of traffic now. Will expand if metrics improve. Bridge: https://meetings.internal/bridge/inc-1812345678

Ben K: Canary shows reduced memory pressure on the canary workers. Error rate on canary down to 1.2%. Expanding to 40% now.

Carlos: Adding testing checklist for RCA: collect worker-level cgroups memory, model artifact sizes, kernel/drivers, autoscaler events, request IDs for failed requests (attach logs). Ben, can you upload a zipped trace to the incident folder?

Ben K: Uploaded: https://internal.storage/incidents/1812345678/trace-kv-oom.tar.gz. Contains worker coredumps and alloc stats.

Jay (oncall): Customer impact note for stakeholders: 2 customers reported timeouts, broad transient errors affecting ~12% of gen requests between 10:29–10:34 UTC. Immediate mitigation: fallback rollout + cache eviction. Status page draft v2: "We mitigated elevated error rates by rolling back to a compatible model variant for a subset of traffic and evicting worker KV caches; normal service restored for most customers by 10:35 UTC. We continue to investigate root cause (KV memory accounting under increased QPS with specific model variant)."

Elena (PM): I'm preparing stakeholder update: will send to CS, Sales, and Security. Timeline + impact + action items: please confirm final numbers and attach logs. Target notify at 11:00 UTC.

Sophie (support): Confirming both flagged customers have been notified and offered credits. CS asked for postmortem timeline when available.

Alice M: Hypotheses to track in RCA thread: (A) model variant increases KV footprint -> OOM on workers under burst; (B) autoscaler scale-up timing caused hot shards -> cache thrash; (C) latent memory leak in runtime. We'll prioritize (A) given canary results.

Jay (oncall): Assigning follow-ups: Ben to analyze artifact memory profile (due +6h), Carlos to correlate autoscaler logs with topology (+3h), Alice to run synthetic burst test with old vs new artifact (+4h). I'll draft initial incident timeline and send to stakeholders.

Ben K: Noted. I'll include a memory comparison table in my writeup.

Carlos: I'll scrape autoscaler events and produce a per-pool graph.

Jay (oncall): Final note: status page posted at 10:42 UTC (minor update) then 11:05 UTC full incident update with mitigation and next steps. If we confirm root cause, we'll coordinate change windows for model artifact rollout policy.

IncidentBot: Incident inc-2026-03-15-01 status changed to "mitigated" at 10:36:05 UTC.

Elena (PM): Thanks team. I'll consolidate and draft the comms bundle for execs. Please add any missing timeline items in the shared doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/1812345678/timeline

Jay (oncall): Adding last note: Postmortem owners: Jay (oncall) lead, Ben K (memory analysis), Alice M (repro & tests), Carlos (scaling analysis), Sophie (customer comms).
